source.title: Why ResNet Works? Residuals Generalize
source.authors: Fengxiang He; Tong-Liang Liu; D. Tao

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops theoretical covering-number and generalization bounds for residual networks. It does not test the empirical behaviors named in V1–V8; the residual-versus-chain result is not a test of the listed convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison in V3.
record.gate_note: The paper states a theoretical result that residual connections may not increase hypothesis-space complexity compared with a chain-like network when the total numbers of weight matrices and nonlinearities are fixed. It does not report a new empirical test-error comparison. Its discussion of weight decay and loss-surface results cites prior work; those results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives covering-number and margin-based generalization bounds for residual networks. Its own results do not address V1–V8. Residual versus chain-like architectures is a different comparison from V3; random-label fitting and sharpness findings are discussed through prior work. Figure 3 reproduces results from Li et al., rather than reporting new experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' conclusions: they derive covering-number bounds for networks with residual connections and a margin-based generalization bound for ResNet, argue that residual connections need not increase hypothesis complexity, and motivate weight decay through the bound's dependence on weight norms. These are theoretical conclusions, not demonstrated improvements in held-out accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis of covering numbers and generalization bounds; no empirical training recipe is compared.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 bounds residual-network covering numbers through products of stem and vine covering factors. Identity vines contribute a factor of one conditional on their input, although vines can influence the stem factors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connections admit a covering-number bound with the same layerwise product structure as chain-like networks; this does not establish equal actual complexity or held-out performance.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The relevant findings are theoretical bounds, not empirical measurements of test error or the training-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No empirical findings are reported by this study. The loss-surface and weight-decay test-error values discussed in Section 5.4 and Figure 3 are identified as results originally presented in cited work [30], so they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Original comparisons of batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with measured generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reproduced batch-size, weight-decay and loss-landscape results in Section 5.4 and Figure 3 are explicitly attributed to Li et al. and already declared in rows_left_out; they warrant neither new rows nor verdicts for this study.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their association with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: Deep neural networks with residual connections under the stem-vine framework
rows.size_stated: Total numbers of weight matrices and nonlinearities fixed
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical comparison of covering-number upper bounds for residual and chain-like networks
rows.measure: Upper bound on hypothesis-space covering number
rows.value: The upper bound remains the same, regardless of whether weight matrices are in residual connections or the stem.
rows.note: This is a theoretical bound, not an empirical test-error measurement.
rows.check: This is a theoretical bound, not a measurement of any listed version. The abstract states the recorded invariance claim, but Section 5.1 qualifies it: vines can influence the stem's covering-number factors, and that cross-influence remains open. Describe the result as a shared product-form upper bound, without implying equal actual hypothesis complexity or test performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
